title: GitHub repo: protection and Actions secrets
summary: Protect the main branch and add the secrets the deploy workflows need.
why: Tags and GitHub Releases are the project's backup; a force-push to main or a deletion would corrupt that history. The web/panel deploy runs in GitHub Actions on a tag and reads the FTP/Firebase credentials from secrets (RULES.md Sections 15.9, 12.6).
prerequisites: The repo should have been created by Claude with `gh repo create --private` (if that failed, first create a **private** repo at github.com/new and enter its URL below).

steps.title: Repo → **Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New branch ruleset**
steps.detail: Name: `main`, Enforcement: **Active**, Target: **Include default branch**. Check: **Restrict deletions**, **Block force pushes**, **Require status checks to pass** → `CI`. Click **Create**.

steps.title: Protect tags too
steps.detail: **New tag ruleset** → Target: the `**/v*` pattern → **Restrict deletions** + **Restrict updates** (tags are immutable).

steps.title: Add the secrets: **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret**
steps.detail: Hostinger: `HOSTINGER_FTP_SERVER`, `HOSTINGER_FTP_USERNAME`, `HOSTINGER_FTP_PASSWORD` · Firebase: `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` · Supabase: `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`. Claude will list the values for you from the relevant records.

fields.label: The main and tag protection rules are **active**
The required Actions secrets have been added
